The Grand Chamber ruled on 21 November 2001, by 9 votes to 8, that there was no violation of Article 6(1). It held that the UK's grant of state immunity to Kuwait pursued a legitimate aim and was proportionate. In effect, immunity trumped the right of access to a court, because international law at the time did not recognize a torture exception to state immunity in civil claims. This matches the second option in the team note.
